_note: U02 gestures - the renderer-neutral pure core behind on:pinch / on:pinchEnd, on:rotate / on:rotateEnd, on:swipe, on:hover / on:hoverEnd, on:pressIn / on:pressOut, the additive on:drag velocity+translation payload, and the COMPOSITION resolver behind gesture= and gestureAxis= (parity/U02-gestures.md). Every section is a pure fold or a renderer-neutral state machine: the platform adapter owns raw touch delivery, pointer identity and its own intent delays, then reports normalized samples here, exactly as input/tooltip.json splits the hover-intent delay from the show/dismiss machine. Units are density-independent (points on Apple targets, dp on Android, CSS px on web) and velocities are units per SECOND. The phase vocabulary is the shipped on:drag one - start | move | end - and a cancelled gesture delivers phase end, which is already the declared cross-renderer law for on:drag. Floating point compares within constants.tolerance.

constants._note: Recognition thresholds and the velocity window, pinned so a spring driven by velocity settles identically on three renderers. tapSlop/axisSlop are the iOS pan slop; swipe needs BOTH a minimum distance and a minimum speed along its own axis.

velocity._note: velocity1D - the ONE derivation every gesture uses (drag, swipe, pinch scale, rotate radians). Weighted moving average over the samples inside the last velocityWindowMs, capped at velocitySamples, oldest pair weighted 1 and each newer pair one more; a pair whose dt <= 0 is DROPPED (never a divide by zero, never Infinity) and fewer than two usable samples is 0.

press._note: on:pressIn / on:pressOut - the custom press-state channel, and the slop that separates a tap from a drag. pressOut ALWAYS balances pressIn (release, cancellation, unmount); a press that exceeded the slop is a drag and never also reports a tap; the slop is radial and one-way (coming back inside does not undo it); one pointer owns the press.

hover._note: on:hover - the POSITIONAL hover channel that complements the shipped on:hoverStart / on:hoverEnd pair (input/hover.json owns pointer identity and the balanced pair; this owns the { x, y } stream). Only a hover-capable source is ever tracked, so a touch screen never fires it and content is never gated behind hover (Article 7). The enter IS the first sample, the on:drag minimum-distance-0 rule.

swipe._note: on:swipe - direction classification at the end of a pan. The DOMINANT axis wins and an exact |dx| == |dy| diagonal breaks HORIZONTAL (the same tie-break the axis claim uses, so a diagonal can never resolve one way here and the other there). Both gates are read along the chosen axis: distance >= swipeMinDistance AND |velocity| >= swipeMinVelocity, which is what makes a slow drag not a swipe. A gestureAxis claim of x or y rejects the other axis outright. The reported distance and velocity are the chosen axis's, positive.

axisClaim._note: gestureAxis= as the RECOGNIZER-LEVEL claim, not a direction check in the handler: until the movement passes axisSlop the recognizer is pending (it has claimed nothing and an ancestor scroll may still take the touch); past the slop an x or y claimer either claims the touch or FAILS, handing it back to the ancestor. This is the iOS UIPanGestureRecognizer-subclass technique and the web touch-action: pan-y declaration, expressed once. Ties break horizontal, exactly as the swipe resolver.

transform._note: The ONE tracker behind on:pinch and on:rotate (Compose detectTransformGestures, UIPinch + UIRotation together): each update carries the FULL set of pointers currently down, and the two lowest-sorted ids define the span. The gesture spans from the first two-pointer engagement until the LAST pointer lifts - dropping to one finger SUSPENDS (values hold, nothing is emitted) and a returning finger re-baselines against the held accumulation, which is why the scale never jumps at a finger change. Rotation accumulates normalized deltas, so it is continuous across the +-pi wrap and keeps growing past a full turn. A re-baseline never emits; start fires the first frame past pinchSlop or rotateSlop; end fires once, with the last values, on the final lift or a cancel. Velocities are the SAME velocity1D fold over the scale and rotation series.

Every shipped key (x, y, width, height, fraction, fractionY, dx, dy, phase) keeps its exact meaning and value; translationX / translationY are the named twins of dx / dy (the gesture-handler vocabulary authors expect) and velocityX / velocityY come from the same velocity1D fold. width and height floor at 1 so a zero-sized element never divides by zero.

composition._note: The composition resolver behind gesture= and gestureAxis=: given the ancestor chain (root first) and one attempt, which recognizers may fire together. The attempt is what the RAW input physically matches - the adapter decides that, this decides composition. Rules in order: (1) a directional recognizer on a node claiming x or y is eliminated when the attempt runs on the other axis; (2) an outstanding claim by one node cancels every other node's recognizers; (3) a gesture=defer node yields while ANY ancestor candidate is still viable; (4) the DEEPEST surviving node owns the touch, and an ancestor keeps its recognizers only if it declared gesture=simultaneous; (5) inside a node the CONTINUOUS recognizers (pinch, rotate, pan, scroll) are exclusive by precedence unless the node declared simultaneous, while discrete ones (tap, longPress, swipe) never compete. fire[] and blocked[] are ordered root to leaf, then by precedence.
